passage:
Instead of giving candy on her birthday, Ms. Chen gave each student a small plant.
Some students were excited. Others worried they would forget to water it. Ms. Chen said they only had to try.
A month later, the plants looked different. Some were tall and green. Some were small. One had died. The class talked about sunlight, water, soil, and care.
Ms. Chen did not make the student with the dead plant feel bad. She said, "A dead plant can still teach a living lesson."
The birthday gift lasted longer than candy. It made students notice growth, responsibility, and the quiet needs of living things.
